subject: Post-call: Dedicated capacity perf validation — latency/concurrency targets
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Chen <samantha@finco.com>, Tom Rivers <tomr@finco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-07T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity perf targets and next steps

Hi Samantha / Tom,

Thanks again for the call today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on requirements for the dedicated capacity validation: 

What you told us
- Target p95 latency: 250ms (end-to-end) for short interactive prompts when streaming tokens.
- Average prompt length: ~40 tokens, typical responses ~80 tokens (so ~120 tokens total turn).
- Expected sustained throughput: 200 requests/sec, with burst concurrency up to 150.
- Must support server-side streaming (SSE/Chunked) so UI shows token-by-token responses.
- Fault-tolerance: graceful fallback to smaller model variant if capacity constrained.

Questions we asked you to confirm
- Can you share a representative prompt set and a small corpus for load testing?
- Do you have a preferred target for 99th percentile or just p95?

Preliminary sizing thoughts
- For the SLOs above we recommend evaluating H100-based nodes for lowest latency, and comparing to A100 to understand cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Reserve throughput: propose a baseline reserved throughput of 250 rps to cover sustained plus buffer; can scale up if needed.

Next steps (proposed)
1) You send sample prompts + expected sequence length + any streaming handshake requirements (tokenization/byte limits).
2) We run an internal perf run comparing: H100 80GB vs A100 80GB, with and without int8 quantization, and measure p50/p95/p99 streaming latencies and tokens/sec.
3) We share a perf matrix and a sizing_estimate.csv for reserved capacity pricing.
4) Schedule a joint validation test where we run your workload from a staging account.

I’ve cc’d Marissa and Aditya to coordinate the validation plan and timeline. If this matches your expectations, I’ll send a proposed test date range.

Thanks,
Rafael
Senior Account Executive\Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Chen <samantha@finco.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Rivers <tomr@finco.com>
Date: 2027-06-08T09:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity perf targets and next steps

Thanks Rafael — that matches our understanding. A few clarifications and items from our side: 

- Prompt details: average prompt tokens ~40, responses ~80 is correct. We will attach a 200-sample prompt set for the perf test.
- p95 target: we care most about p95 for interactive UI; p99 is nice-to-have but not mandatory initially.
- Streaming: yes — SSE is required. We’ll need latency for first token (TTFB) and p95 for end-to-end response.
- Concurrency: we see bursts to 150, sustained 200 rps during daytime for parts of the app.
- Security: attaching the completed security questionnaire per your request.

We are interested in H100 if it materially reduces p95 for our short-response use case, but cost will be a big factor. Please include both perf and cost comparisons.

Tom and I are available for a joint run the week of June 14.

Best,
Samantha Chen\Product Manager, FinCo

Attachments: finco_security_questionnaire.pdf

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Chen <samantha@finco.com>, Tom Rivers <tomr@finco.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-08T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity perf targets and next steps

Marissa / Aditya — forwarding Samantha’s confirmation and the questionnaire. Key updates: sustained 200 rps, bursts to 150 concurrent users, SSE required, p95 target 250ms for typical short responses.

Ask: can infra/SE run a quick sizing with both H100 and A100 baseline configurations and produce a perf matrix (p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization) and a sizing_estimate.csv we can send FinCo? Also include cost delta for reserved H100 vs A100 capacity.

Proposed test week: June 14 — can we schedule internal prep next Tue to align the harness?

Thanks,
Rafael
--- Forwarded message attached ---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Chen <samantha@finco.com>, Tom Rivers <tomr@finco.com>
Date: 2027-06-09T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity perf targets and next steps

Thanks Rafael — I’ll own the validation plan. High-level approach below; attaching a test plan workbook with test matrix.

Validation plan (summary)
- Goals: validate p95 streaming latency <= 250ms, measure TTFB and end-to-end p95/p99, and determine reserved throughput sizing for 200rps sustained.
- Test cases:
  1) Baseline: A100 80GB, batch_size=1, no quantization
  2) A100 80GB, int8 quantization
  3) H100 80GB, batch_size=1, no quantization
  4) H100 80GB, int8 quantization (if supported)
  5) Concurrency sweep: ramp concurrent connections 10 -> 300 to find p95 inflection point
  6) Streaming latency measurement: measure time-to-first-token and per-token latency while streaming 80-token responses
- Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 (ms), TTFB (ms), tokens/sec, GPU utilization (%), memory pressure, dropped/errored requests.
- Acceptance criteria: p95 <= 250ms for configured workload on chosen config; stable throughput with <1% error rate.
- Deliverables: perf_matrix.xlsx, sizing_estimate.csv, run logs, and a short recommendation note (H100 vs A100 tradeoffs).

Prep needed from FinCo
- 200-sample prompt set (Samantha to send)
- Any rate-limiting/auth nuances for streaming connections

Timeline
- Wed June 9: internal prep call between SE + infra to finalize harness
- Week of June 14: perf runs (2–3 days)
- By June 18: deliverables and recommendation to FinCo

I’ve attached perf_test_plan_v1.xlsx and a draft sizing_estimate.csv. Aditya — can you coordinate the infra run and ensure we capture GPU-level telemetry? Neha — please help with cost delta and pricing language for reserved throughput.

Cheers,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: perf_test_plan_v1.xlsx, sizing_estimate.csv

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Chen <samantha@finco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Confirming test week and data needs

Samantha — thanks for confirming the week of June 14. We’ll do internal prep Wed June 9 (Marissa/Aditya/infra). Final plan below and ask from FinCo before the run: 

- Deliverables we’ll provide: perf_matrix.xlsx, sizing_estimate.csv, recommended reserved throughput (baseline 250 rps), and cost delta H100 vs A100.
- What we need from FinCo by June 11 EOD:
  * 200-sample prompt set (representative of critical flows)
  * Any auth tokens/test account details and rate-limit headers to replicate production behavior
  * Confirmation on whether initial rollout can accept int8 quantization (if not, note in reply)

If you approve, we’ll schedule the joint validation run for Tues June 15–16 and will share a calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this validated.

Best,
Rafael
Senior Account Executive\Redwood Inference
